decisions.rationale: Hematoma of the spermatic cord is unlikely given the absence of trauma history and the solid, well-demarcated nature of the mass on ultrasonography.
Granuloma is not a likely diagnosis given the lack of inflammation or infection history and the appearance of the mass on ultrasonography.
Sarcoma is unlikely given the benign appearance of the mass on ultrasonography and the lack of aggressive features.
Seminoma is a type of testicular cancer, but the mass is localized to the epididymis and has a benign appearance on ultrasonography.
Metastatic tumor is unlikely given the lack of known primary cancer and the benign appearance of the mass on ultrasonography.
Lipoma is a type of benign tumor, but the mass has a solid, well-demarcated appearance on ultrasonography that is not typical of lipoma.
None is not a valid diagnosis given the presence of a palpable mass and ultrasonography findings.
